arguments.value: S. Maurice Hicks, Jr. is a United States district judge for the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Louisiana, where he has served since his confirmation in 2003 and as chief judge from 2017 to 2022. Born in New Orleans in 1952, he earned his B.A. from Texas Christian University in 1974 and his J.D. from Louisiana State University Law School in 1977. Before joining the bench, he worked as a law clerk and staff attorney for the Louisiana Legislative Council and practiced privately in Shreveport from 1977 to 2003. He was nominated to the federal bench by President George W. Bush, confirmed by the Senate in May 2003, and later served on the Judicial Conference of the United States from 2020 to 2023.
